title: Machine learning helps recover dimension from quantum periods for a class of Fano varieties
summary: A feed-forward neural network classified the dimension of Fano varieties from quantum-period coefficients with 98% accuracy on the authors’ dataset. The authors report that machine learning helped formulate rigorous asymptotic results, which prove dimension recovery for specified low-Picard-rank toric Fano classes. The broader conjecture that the quantum period uniquely determines every Fano variety remains open; the empirical classification accuracy is not itself a proof. The journal article appeared 2023-09-08, before the same work’s 2023-09-11 arXiv posting.
organization: Imperial College London; University of Nottingham

source_review.scope: Primary author-hosted full manuscript plus primary publisher article metadata; checked authors, method, theorem scope and chronology.

evidence.tested: The article combines a dataset classification result with rigorous asymptotic proofs for specified classes.
evidence.unknown: 98% is empirical accuracy on the paper’s dataset; the broad uniqueness conjecture remains open. Journal publication preceded arXiv submission.
evidence.ai_role: A neural network analyzed quantum-period coefficients and helped identify dimension-related patterns used to formulate asymptotic results, which the authors prove for restricted classes.
